scope: On principal elliptic bundles over compact Kahler surfaces, a nonzero nonnegative curvature square Q=alpha^2+beta^2 gives the exact cubic bounded-potential lower mass and the quantitative determinant endpoint over all normalized singular and degenerate Gauduchon currents for every Hermitian background. Explicit non-Hopf line-bundle quotients and a separately reconstructed Calabi-Eckmann no-LCK example verify the hypotheses. Primitive curvature has the opposite sign. The general-dimensional and unrestricted primitive-bundle problems remain open.

final_source_bindings_full_root_read.statement: Bedford–Taylor, A new capacity for plurisubharmonic functions (1982), Section 2, equation (2.1), Theorem 2.1 and Corollary 2.2: for locally bounded canonical psh functions v1,...,vk on an open subset of C^N, 1≤k≤N, the recursively defined product dd^c v1∧...∧dd^c vk is a closed positive order-zero current, symmetric and multilinear in the functions, and these mixed products converge weakly under decreasing locally uniformly bounded psh approximations with locally bounded canonical psh limits.
final_source_bindings_full_root_read.quote: into the cone of nonnegative closed currents

final_source_bindings_full_root_read.statement: Bedford–Taylor (1982), Theorem 2.4: if v_j^0,...,v_j^k are decreasing locally uniformly bounded psh sequences on an open subset of C^N with locally bounded canonical psh limits v^0,...,v^k, then v_j^0 dd^c v_j^1∧...∧dd^c v_j^k converges weakly as an order-zero current to v^0 dd^c v^1∧...∧dd^c v^k, including k=N.
final_source_bindings_full_root_read.quote: where the convergence is as currents of order 0

final_source_bindings_full_root_read.statement: Boucksom–Guedj–Lu, Volumes of Bott–Chern classes, arXiv:2406.01090v1, Section 2.1 and Proposition 2.1: on a compact complex manifold of dimension N, bounded canonical quasi-psh functions have well-defined closed signed order-zero mixed dd^c products. For arbitrary smooth real (1,1)-forms θ_i and bounded canonical quasi-psh functions φ_i, 1≤p≤N, smooth-factor expansion defines a symmetric multilinear order-zero product of T_i=θ_i+dd^c φ_i, independent of their smooth decompositions; this product is positive when every T_i is positive. These bounded-product statements do not require the bounded mass property.
final_source_bindings_full_root_read.quote: one easily checks that (2.2) only depends on the currents

Angella–Guedj–Lu, Plurisigned hermitian metrics, arXiv:2207.04705v1, Definition 3.1 and Theorem 3.2, already state the following three-dimensional lower-mass result: if a compact complex threefold has a smooth Hermitian form ω with dd^c(ω²)=0 and dd^c ω≤0, then v_−(ω)=∫_X ω³>0, with v_− defined over bounded genuine ω-psh potentials.
final_source_bindings_full_root_read.quote: If X admits a hermitian metric ω that satisfies Plurineg(n)

final_source_bindings_full_root_read.statement: Angella–Guedj–Lu, arXiv:2207.04705v1, Proposition 3.10, states that for a compact Hermitian manifold locally conformally Kähler with potential π*ω=dd^c φ/φ, where φ is smooth positive psh on the universal cover and transforms by positive constants under deck transformations, the additional Vaisman hypothesis implies dd^c ω≤0 and v_−(ω)>0 when its complex dimension is three.
